acceptance: One CI run per push for the CI workflow (the separate cheap CI (text edit) run is by design); met by #3434's per-PR concurrency and dedupe

DROPPED by owner 2026-10-25: stuck-run alert. Study of 16,209 runs (2026-10-11 to 10-25) found 325 jobless waits over 15 min, all explained (Trunk queue 285, cancelled-run summary jobs 22, own-group queue 10, approval 7, one artifact), zero truly stuck; merge delay at most 0.6 h in two weeks
context:
OWNER DECISION 2026-10-25: alert criterion dropped on the study evidence (zero truly stuck runs); item closed. The one real delay source, cancelled runs' summary jobs holding runner slots, is filed as ci-cancelled-run-summary-jobs-hold-slots-20261025, together with the dedupe-test gap.

Merged PR #3434: gitignore-lint.yml gained a per-PR cancel-in-progress concurrency group, and tests/unit/workflows/test_workflow_dispatch_dedupe.py now forbids overlapping push+pull_request triggers and requires a per-PR/per-ref cancel-in-progress group on every pull_request workflow. The observed duplicate (CI on opened plus `CI (text edit)` seconds later) is the deliberate edited-event verdict-copy design and was left alone. NOT done: automatic cancel/alert of stuck jobless ghost runs. A watchdog was built and dropped because the Actions API reports a run queued behind a concurrency group the same as a stuck jobless run (queued/pending, zero jobs) and does not expose the group, so cancelling could drop real CI runs. A safe watchdog needs another signal (e.g. runner-side or org-level data); item stays open for that.
description: Every push spawns two CI workflow runs ~13s apart; on 2026-10-12 a jobless ghost run (pending, zero jobs) held its concurrency group and stalled scheduling repo-wide ~45 min until manually cancelled + rerun. Seen on fix/revert-2821 and feat/tuning-merge-settle-recorded.
